heart-anterior.prompt: Draw the heart, anterior view. Label the 4 chambers, the great vessels and the valves.
heart-anterior.clinical_context: The sternocostal surface is critical in emergency medicine (pericardiocentesis, trauma, ECG lead placement). The right ventricle constitutes the vast majority of the anterior silhouette, while the left ventricle forms the apex pointing inferolaterally to the patient's left.

required_structures.name: Right Ventricle
required_structures.relative_position: Center and lower right of the cardiac silhouette; forms the vast majority of the anterior/sternocostal surface
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Large; occupies approximately 40-50% of the visible anterior ventricular area

required_structures.name: Left Ventricle
required_structures.relative_position: Anatomical left border (viewer's right); forms the inferior-lateral margin and cardiac apex
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Moderate anteriorly; occupies approximately 20-25% of visible anterior surface (narrow strip and apex)

required_structures.name: Right Atrium and Auricle
required_structures.relative_position: Anatomical right margin (viewer's left), superior to the right ventricle; auricle overlaps the proximal ascending aorta
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Moderate; approximately 15-20% of anterior cardiac mass

required_structures.name: Left Auricle
required_structures.relative_position: Visible on the anatomical left shoulder of the heart, immediately lateral to the base of the pulmonary trunk
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Small; approximately 5% of anterior cardiac surface

required_structures.name: Pulmonary Trunk
required_structures.relative_position: Originates from the infundibulum of the right ventricle, anterior and slightly leftward relative to the ascending aorta
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Moderate vessel caliber; comparable in diameter to the ascending aorta

required_structures.name: Ascending Aorta & Arch
required_structures.relative_position: Emerges posterior to the pulmonary trunk, curves superiorly and toward the anatomical left, giving off three brachiocephalic branches
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Large prominent vascular trunk; spans superior midline

required_structures.name: Superior Vena Cava (SVC)
required_structures.relative_position: Vertical vessel on the anatomical right, entering the superior aspect of the right atrium, lateral to the ascending aorta
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Moderate vessel caliber; slightly narrower than ascending aorta

required_structures.name: Apex of the Heart
required_structures.relative_position: Inferior-most tip of the left ventricle, oriented inferolaterally toward the anatomical left (viewer's right)
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Focal point/landmark; formed entirely by left ventricle

required_structures.name: Anterior Interventricular Sulcus
required_structures.relative_position: Groove running obliquely from near the pulmonary base down toward the apex (terminating just right of the apex)
required_structures.typical_size_relative_to_whole: Linear boundary spanning across the lower two-thirds of the ventricular mass

key_relationships.relationship_description: The pulmonary trunk must arise anterior to the ascending aorta; the aorta arches over the right pulmonary artery and posterior to the bifurcation of the pulmonary trunk.

key_relationships.structure_pair: Superior Vena Cava and Right Atrium
key_relationships.relationship_description: The SVC must connect directly into the superior-posterior aspect of the right atrium without crossing other major vessels.
The right ventricle must dominate the sternocostal surface; the left ventricle is separated by the anterior interventricular sulcus and forms the apex.
Three distinct branches must originate along the superior convexity of the arch in strict anatomical sequence from right to left: Brachiocephalic trunk, Left Common Carotid, Left Subclavian.
The right auricle wraps around the base of the ascending aorta; the left auricle projects anteriorly adjacent to the left of the pulmonary trunk.

common_student_mistakes.visual_sign: Drawing the left ventricle on the viewer's left and right ventricle on the viewer's right (failing to use anatomical orientation).
Drawing the ascending aorta emerging anteriorly to the pulmonary trunk, rather than emerging posterior-rightward to it.
Drawing the left ventricle as the dominant anterior surface instead of the right ventricle, neglecting that the LV is predominantly posterior/lateral.
Placing the apex in the midline or pointing toward the anatomical right, or depicting it as being formed by the right ventricle.

common_student_mistakes.error_description: Branching errors of the aortic arch
common_student_mistakes.visual_sign: Drawing four branches, omitting the brachiocephalic trunk, or drawing symmetric paired common carotids directly off the arch.
